tensions.description: Packer's claim that Shannon Bell murdered the other men while Packer was away scouting directly contradicts coroner reports stating all five victims were struck in the head while asleep, as well as forensic marks suggesting defensive wounds.

Packer's assertion of shooting Shannon Bell in self-defense is complicated by forensic analysis showing defensive marks on Bell's bones, yet supported by the discovery of a revolver matching lead in Bell's hip.
Divergence between Packer's conviction for murder and modern scientific/forensic findings suggesting he acted in self-defense.

Packer claimed to have killed Shannon Bell in self-defense and eaten companions out of unavoidable starvation, whereas crime scene analysis showed all victims killed in a single location with signs of defensive wounds and unconsumed flesh remaining.

Forensic evidence verifies that Shannon Bell was indeed shot with lead matching Packer's firearm, supporting part of Packer's account, yet skeletal defensive trauma suggests a violent assault on the party members.
Tension between legal/official condemnation (refusal of pardon, conviction) and public/popular celebration (naming grills, holding annual traditions).
Contradictions across Packer's own statements regarding whether deaths were mutual survival cannibalism or single-handed murder by Shannon Bell.
The tension between institutional efforts to correct historical errors with facts versus the public's desire to preserve entertaining Western lore.
The tension between Packer's historical account of necessary survival cannibalism/self-defense and the physical forensic evidence showing lethal violence and systematic defleshing.
The tension between historical efforts to sympathize with or pardon Packer and the conclusive guilt asserted by modern forensic investigators.
Tension between the physical evidence from exhumations suggesting a single massacre site and Packer's testimony of self-defense during extreme starvation.
Tension between the official conviction/public view of Packer as a calculating murderer versus the argument that prejudice and mental distress led to an unfair judgment.
Discrepancies exist between historical records of Pry's marital status and personal life versus cinematic depictions that omitted her marriage to construct a romantic storyline.
Discrepancy between Packer's self-defense and survival account versus the physical evidence, spending behavior, and public suspicion that led to murder convictions.

Packer claimed self-defense and accidental stranding based on Chief Ouray's advice, whereas physical evidence showed hatchet fractures to skulls and witness accounts proved Ouray warned them of severe snow hazards.
Public and official warnings (such as Governor Adams') against supporting a convicted cannibal contrasted with external romanticization and active legal advocacy by Pry and Newman.
